questions.title: Who will win the 2026 special election for California's 14th congressional district?
questions.background: A special election will fill the U.S. House vacancy created by Eric Swalwell's resignation in April 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Consistent winner projections reported by major U.S. news organizations based on special-election results. Resolution Event : Resolve when a winner is publicly projected for the special election to complete Swalwell's unexpired term. The November 2026 election for the following full term does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major spending and endorsement shift ahead of the Aug 18 CA-14 special runoff (The American Prospect Aug 5, Independent News July 30, East Bay Insiders July 20-22): since July 1, pro-Israel and moderate super PACs (led by AIPAC-backed BOLD America at $1.485M and United Democracy Project at $850k+) have poured $2.45M in outside spending for Melissa Hernandez / against Aisha Wahab—over 12-to-1 compared to <$200k for Wahab—on top of $570k+ in Hernandez campaign TV/cable buys targeting Wahab on public safety (SB 1414), and sources tell The American Prospect the race is tightening as mail ballots are out. Hernandez has also consolidated every CA-14 mayor and county supervisor, local police and firefighter unions, Teamsters Joint Council 7, and Bay Area Reps. Liccardo, Gray, and Lofgren. Still, Wahab remains a solid favorite after beating Hernandez by >20 points twice in June (38.3%-17.2% June 2; 42.8%-16.8% June 16 special primary) with backing from the California Democratic Party, SEIU, California Labor Federation, and NNU. Lowering Aisha Wahab 0.83 -> 0.72 and raising Melissa Hernandez 0.17 -> 0.28 to reflect the massive 12-to-1 summer special-election spending blitz and reported tightening.

questions.title: Which Ukrainian suspect, if any, will be arrested in August 2026 in connection with Germany's investigation into the Nord Stream pipeline bombings?
questions.background: Germany is investigating the September 2022 explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines. A former Ukrainian army officer was arrested in Italy in August 2025 and transferred to Germany that November.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Confirmation from German federal prosecutors or the authorities carrying out the arrest, as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the Ukrainian suspect physically arrested during August 2026 pursuant to a German warrant concerning the September 2022 Nord Stream pipeline bombings. The issuance of a warrant without an actual arrest does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The suspect's full name. If no qualifying arrest occurs during August 2026, answer “None”.
questions.current_reasoning: Major time-decay and July-August investigative update (first refresh since June 24): (1) 11 of 31 days of August 2026 (35.5% of the resolution window) have already elapsed with zero qualifying arrests reported in Exa Snapshot or local wires through 2026-08-11 — pure constant-hazard survival from our 0.65 prior lifts 'None' to ~0.76 for the remaining 20 days. (2) On July 1-2, German federal prosecutors formally indicted detained former Ukrainian officer Serhii K. in Hamburg (trial this autumn) on war-crimes/sabotage charges, prompting Ukraine's Prosecutor General to publicly deny Kyiv involvement on July 9 (Tagesschau/DW/BBC/AP/Reuters). High-profile publicity around Serhii K.'s Aug 2025 Rimini arrest and German EAW enforcement strongly deters remaining at-large suspects from EU summer travel. (3) Tagesschau (July 1) also noted 1 of the 7 identified Andromeda suspects (a soldier) was killed in the war against Russia, further shrinking the arrestable pool. Raise 'None' 0.65 -> 0.75 (still leaving 25% for a surprise late-August travel arrest). Among named suspects, hold Roman Chervinskyi at 0.06 (boosted relatively after ZDF frontal July 25 revealed Serhii K. implicated 'Kommandeur Roman' in wiretapped prison phone calls cited in the 108-page indictment, though he likely remains inside Ukraine) alongside Volodymyr Zhuravlov 0.08 -> 0.06 (Polish court previously refused extradition), Yevhen Uspenskyi 0.04 -> 0.03, and Svitlana Uspenska 0.03 -> 0.02 (sum = 0.92, 8% residual for other unnamed crew).

questions.title: Which armed group will the United States explicitly identify as an Iranian proxy in an August 2026 designation update?
questions.background: The United States uses counterterrorism designations and financial sanctions to target armed organizations and their funding networks.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official U.S. Treasury or State Department announcement issued during August 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous reliable reporting. Qualifying Event : The announcement must explicitly update an armed group's existing U.S. designation to identify that group as an Iranian proxy. A statement alleging Iranian support without announcing a designation update does not qualify. Resolution Date : The date the qualifying designation update is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the armed group whose designation is updated.
questions.current_reasoning: The June 2026 US-Iran MOU did not address Iran's regional proxies, creating strong pressure on Treasury and State to use updated terrorism designations in August 2026 to maintain leverage. Updating an existing FTO/SDGT designation to explicitly identify a group as an Iranian proxy points to groups already designated where proxy status is either being newly codified or reinforced—such as the Houthis (redesignated FTO March 2025), Hamas, Al-Shabaab (amid US intelligence on Iran/Houthi weapons transfers), Kata'ib Hezbollah, or Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Because dozens of designated groups could receive an OFAC/State designation update, probabilities are kept calibrated (sum 0.47).

local_articles.title: Carrick seeks to build on revival as Man United chase return to elite

Carrick's greatest achievement was restoring balance and confidence to a squad that had looked disjointed. United became harder to beat, more coherent in possession and far more threatening going forward. questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official Premier League result for Nottingham Forest's first league fixture of the 2026–27 season. Resolution : Resolve according to the result at full time, including stoppage time. Preseason and cup fixtures do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning club's name, or “Draw” if the match finishes level.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1 reporting (Irish Times/Guardian, Straits Times/AFP) confirms Nottingham Forest activated Vitor Pereira's June break clause late Tuesday to sack him and are poised to appoint former Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner on a three-year contract. Glasner—winner of the 2024-25 FA Cup, 2025-26 UEFA Conference League, and 2022 Europa League—is a substantial tactical upgrade over Pereira and arrives more than seven weeks before the August 22 opener at the City Ground, giving him a full preseason plus funds from Elliot Anderson's £116m sale to Manchester City (with Forest already targeting Spurs midfielder Lucas Bergvall). Tempering the boost slightly for Forest's managerial churn (fifth head coach in under a year) and early tactical transition, net Matchday 1 home-win probability rises from 0.44 to 0.47 (Draw 0.28 -> 0.27, Leeds United 0.28 -> 0.26).
